title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Code / Cowork ship fleet-hygiene fixes that hit our exact failure modes — /doctor now diagnoses and repairs, scheduled tasks no longer duplicate-fire on wake, Cowork VM-mode login fixed
bullets.summary: /doctor moved from a read-only report to interactive repair: checks installation health, finds unused skills / MCP servers / plugins weighed against their context cost, deduplicates local CLAUDE.md against checked-in ones, proposes trimming derivable CLAUDE.md content, and flags slow hooks — asking before it changes anything. Alongside: a fix for scheduled tasks firing many duplicate runs at once when the computer wakes from sleep, and a fix for Cowork VM-mode local-agent sessions failing with 'Not logged in / Please run /login' on CLI 2.1.203+.
bullets.how: Maintenance for The Construct's own fleet, not theory. We run a large installed-skills registry and a wide MCP surface, and the context-cost audit is exactly the pruning signal the daily/weekly new-skills scan lacks. The duplicate-fire-on-wake fix matters directly — this brief, the Lens Harvard scan, and the PRAGMA visibility scan are all sleep-straddling scheduled tasks that stood to double-run. Run /doctor against the Construct config this week and let it flag the dead weight.

bullets.title: Anthropic ships Claude for Teachers — the sellable unit is a skills pack + curriculum connections + a data-governance addendum, given away free
bullets.summary: Verified US K-12 educators get free premium Claude access bundled with teaching skills and curriculum connections aligned to standards in all 50 states; Teachers data is excluded from model training and student data is governed by a FERPA-compliant K-12 Data Processing Addendum, with a pilot evaluation in Detroit Public Schools Community District.
bullets.how: Read it as packaging, not education. The vertical bundle is skills + domain data connections + an explicit data-governance instrument — and the governance instrument is what makes it adoptable inside a regulated institution. That's the template for a PRAGMA vertical pack (signage, real estate, contractors): a named skill set, wired-in domain sources, and a written data posture. The addendum is a feature, not paperwork.

bullets.title: Norm Ai raises $120M at a $1.2B valuation to build 'supervisory agents' that audit other AI systems
bullets.summary: Khosla-led, with Blackstone, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, Vanguard, New York Life and Fenwick participating. Norm turns regulatory rules into autonomous agents and is investing in supervisory agents that monitor and audit other AI deployments — its flagship compliance agent runs alongside Microsoft 365 Copilot, flagging missing disclosures, policy conflicts and unsourced claims while maintaining a full audit trail, already serving institutions managing $30T+.
bullets.how: The market is now pricing auditability itself as the product — the same thesis as yesterday's 'Prompts to Contracts' paper, arriving with a $1.2B price tag on it. The agent-that-watches-the-agent is a real PRAGMA product shape for clients running Copilot or ChatGPT Work with no oversight layer. Not our wedge to chase into legal, but strong confirmation the moat is the audit trail, not the model.

bullets.title: GPT-5.6 becomes the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot and auto-enables for all eligible commercial users on July 24 unless an admin blocks it
bullets.summary: The Sol/Terra/Luna family is now default across Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Chat; rollout is opt-out rather than opt-in, with mandatory enablement Jul 24.
bullets.how: The point isn't the model, it's the default. Every SMB client of ours on M365 gets a materially different AI in their Office apps on Jul 24 without asking for it, and most won't notice until output changes. That's a free PRAGMA conversation opener — 'do you know what changed in your Copilot last week, and who decided?' — and a reminder that our own routing stays provider-agnostic precisely so nobody flips our defaults for us.

praxis_lesson: On a quiet frontier day the useful signal is housekeeping and packaging. /doctor's new context-cost audit and the duplicate-fire-on-wake fix mean The Construct's fleet should be pruned and verified this week rather than extended — unused skills and MCP servers are a tax we've been paying silently, and our sleep-straddling scheduled scans were a real duplicate-run risk. Meanwhile Claude for Teachers and Norm Ai's $1.2B say the same thing from opposite ends: the sellable unit is never the model — it's a bounded skill pack plus a written governance posture (Anthropic) or a full audit trail (Norm). PRAGMA should sell the instrument, not the intelligence.
